source.page: From vulnerability discovery to multistep security analysis
source.quote: As part of post-training, we introduced vulnerability discovery data and authorized security environments into the training mix.
They also create clear dual-use risks. We are therefore taking a staged approach to release.

topics.headline: an external classifier identifies high-risk requests and helps prevent clearly harmful activity

source.quote: In our hosted services, an external classifier identifies high-risk requests and helps prevent clearly harmful activity.

topics.headline: adversarial data covering jailbreak variants, disguised intent, and other attempts to evade safety review

source.quote: We also constructed adversarial data covering jailbreak variants, disguised intent, and other attempts to evade safety review.

topics.headline: evaluations cover unauthorized intrusion and other clearly malicious activity; red teams test manipulation into harmful activity

source.quote: These evaluations examine both whether the model can be manipulated into supporting harmful activity and whether its safeguards interfere with legitimate security work.

topics.headline: A reasoning monitor assesses risk during task execution across multiple steps

source.quote: A reasoning monitor assesses risk during task execution. It is designed to detect harmful objectives that may emerge across multiple steps

source.quote: CyberGym begins with white-box source code and tests whether a model can identify and validate vulnerabilities by triggering faults. GLM-5.3 scores 84.5%

topics.headline: universities and professional security teams evaluate GLM models on real-world codebases; partners will red-team before broader release

source.quote: We have also worked with universities and professional security teams to evaluate GLM models on real-world codebases in authorized settings.

testers.scope: evaluate GLM models on real-world codebases in authorized settings

source.quote: We have also worked with universities and professional security teams to evaluate GLM models on real-world codebases in authorized settings.

findings.text: Z.ai cites a prior case where GLM-5.2 helped Hugging Face investigate an AI that autonomously bypassed its own safeguards.

source.quote: When GLM-5.2 helped Hugging Face investigate an incident in which an AI autonomously bypassed its own safeguards, it highlighted a broader shift.

findings.text: Release is staged: selected security partners first, then broader API access, then complete model weights after safety evaluations.

source.quote: Selected security partners will first evaluate GLM-5.3 in controlled settings. Broader access and API availability will follow. Once the necessary safety evaluations and release preparations are complete, we will publish GLM-5.3’s complete model weights.

findings.text: Safeguards use three layers: an external classifier, a reasoning monitor, and deep safety alignment in the model.

source.quote: For GLM-5.3, we use a defense-in-depth approach with three complementary layers.

findings.text: Only model-level alignment ships with the open-weight checkpoint; hosted classifiers and monitors do not.

source.quote: Hosted classifiers and monitors apply to our services, but they do not automatically accompany the model into every local deployment. Model-level alignment is the safety layer included in the released checkpoint.

findings.text: Across authorized real-world evaluations, the GLM series produced 2,436 vulnerability findings in 269 projects, including 1,097 medium-to-high severity.

source.quote: Across this work, the GLM series has produced 2,436 vulnerability findings across 269 projects, including 1,097 categorized as medium-to-high severity.

findings.text: Z.ai created a Security Disclosure Ledger that can publish a cryptographic hash for issues still under coordinated disclosure.

source.page: Discovery must be followed by responsible disclosure
source.quote: For vulnerabilities still under coordinated disclosure, the ledger can publish a cryptographic hash. This allows a finding to be verified later without prematurely revealing operational details.

findings.text: The lab is launching the OpenVuln initiative to help audit open-source projects and support disclosure and remediation.

source.quote: To help address this imbalance, we are launching the OpenVuln initiative alongside GLM-5.3.

findings.text: The lab states that keywords alone cannot reliably tell authorized security work from attack intent.

source.quote: Keywords alone cannot reliably distinguish these cases. Intent, authorization, context, target, and potential impact all matter.

findings.text: The lab says model-level safeguards raise the barrier to abuse but cannot give absolute control once weights are public.

source.quote: Once model weights are public, no developer can guarantee control over every downstream modification or use. Model-level safeguards can raise the barrier to abuse, but they cannot provide absolute control.
